instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine chicken pieces with yogurt, 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice, 1/2 tsp garam masala, turmeric powder, red chili powder, and salt. Mix well to coat the chicken. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or preferably 2-4 hours for best flavor.

instructions.title: Cook the Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 1 tbsp of butter in a large pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken in batches, ensuring not to overcrowd the pan. Cook until browned on all sides and mostly cooked through, about 5-7 minutes per batch. Remove chicken and set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Gravy Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, melt the remaining 3 tbsp of butter. Add chopped onion and green cardamom pods. Sauté until onions are soft and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the remaining 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant.

instructions.title: Simmer the Gravy
instructions.text: Stir in the crushed tomatoes, remaining 1/2 tsp garam masala, and sugar. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 15-20 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the tomatoes to break down. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.

instructions.title: Blend and Finish the Gravy
instructions.text: Drain the soaked cashews and add them to the tomato mixture. Carefully transfer the hot mixture to a blender or use an immersion blender to blend until completely smooth. Strain the gravy through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pan for an extra silky texture. Return to low heat.

instructions.title: Combine and Serve
instructions.text: Add the cooked chicken to the smooth gravy. Stir in the heavy cream and crushed fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi). Simmer gently for another 5-7 minutes, allowing the chicken to absorb the flavors and the gravy to thicken slightly. Do not boil after adding cream. Garnish with fresh cilantro and serve hot.

tips: For the smoothest gravy, ensure you blend the tomato-cashew mixture thoroughly and then pass it through a fine-mesh sieve to remove any fibrous bits.
Adjust the level of sweetness and tanginess to your preference. A pinch more sugar can balance the tomatoes, or a touch more lemon juice can add brightness.
Kasoori methi (dried fenugreek leaves) is crucial for authentic Butter Chicken flavor. Rub it between your palms before adding to release its aroma.
article:
Savor the rich, creamy goodness of Butter Chicken, a dish that has captivated taste buds worldwide and remains a staple among Indian lunch recipes. Known in Hindi as Murgh Makhani, which literally translates to "chicken with butter," this iconic curry is more than just a meal; it's an experience of tender chicken bathed in a velvety, spiced tomato sauce that promises comfort and indulgence in every bite. Whether you're a seasoned chef or a home cook looking to explore the vibrant flavors of India, mastering this dish is a rewarding culinary journey.

## What is Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)?

Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, is a classic Indian curry originating from Delhi in the 1950s. Legend has it that the dish was created by Kundan Lal Gujral, the founder of Moti Mahal restaurant, who experimented with leftover tandoori chicken by simmering it in a rich tomato gravy enriched with butter and cream. The result was a revelation: a mild, tangy, and slightly sweet curry that quickly rose to fame.

At its heart, Butter Chicken features succulent pieces of chicken (often tandoori-style, though pan-fried or baked works beautifully for home cooking) swimming in a luscious, vibrant orange-red sauce. This sauce is typically made from a base of pureed tomatoes, ginger, garlic, and a blend of aromatic spices like garam masala, cumin, and fenugreek leaves (kasuri methi). The generous addition of butter and fresh cream at the end gives the curry its characteristic smooth texture and rich, decadent flavor, making it an irresistible choice for an Indian lunch. Its universal appeal lies in its balanced taste – not overly spicy, yet profoundly flavorful, making it a favorite for all ages.

## Ingredients You'll Need

To embark on your Butter Chicken journey, gather these essential ingredients. This recipe typically serves 4-6 people, perfect for a family lunch or meal prepping.

For the Chicken Marinade:
*   1.5 lbs boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breasts, cut into 1-inch pieces
*   1/2 cup plain yogurt
*   1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste
*   1 tsp red chili powder (Kashmiri chili powder for color, less heat)
*   1/2 tsp turmeric powder
*   1/2 tsp garam masala
*   Salt to taste

For the Gravy:
*   2 tbsp unsalted butter + 1 tbsp for finishing
*   1 large onion, finely chopped
*   1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste
*   1 (28 oz) can crushed tomatoes or 4-5 large fresh tomatoes, pureed
*   1/2 cup raw cashews (soaked in warm water for 15-20 minutes, optional but recommended for smoothness)
*   1/2 cup water or chicken broth
*   1 tsp red chili powder
*   1 tsp garam masala
*   1/2 tsp turmeric powder
*   1 tsp sugar (or to taste, balances acidity)
*   1 tsp dried fenugreek leaves (kasuri methi), crushed
*   1/2 cup heavy cream
*   Salt to taste
*   Fresh cilantro, chopped, for garnish

## Step-by-Step Instructions for Butter Chicken

Making this delicious Butter Chicken is easier than you think. Follow these steps for a perfect meal:

1.  **Marinate the Chicken:** In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with all the marinade ingredients. Mix well to ensure the chicken is evenly coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or preferably 2-4 hours, to allow the flavors to penetrate.

2.  **Cook the Chicken:** Heat a little oil or butter in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken in batches, ensuring not to overcrowd the pan. Cook until browned on all sides and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes per batch. Set aside.

3.  **Prepare the Gravy Base:** In the same pan, melt 2 tablespoons of butter over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant.

4.  **Simmer the Gravy:** Stir in the crushed tomatoes (or fresh tomato puree), soaked cashews, red chili powder, turmeric powder, and garam masala. Add 1/2 cup of water or chicken broth. Bring the mixture to a simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes are well cooked and the sauce has thickened slightly.

5.  **Blend the Gravy:** Carefully transfer the cooked gravy mixture to a blender. Blend until completely smooth. If needed, add a splash more water to achieve a creamy consistency. You can also pass the blended sauce through a fine-mesh sieve for an extra silky texture, though this step is optional.

6.  **Finish the Butter Chicken:** Pour the smooth gravy back into the pan. Stir in the cooked chicken pieces, sugar, and dried fenugreek leaves (crush them between your palms before adding to release their aroma). Simmer for another 5-10 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the chicken to absorb the sauce.

7.  **Add the Finishing Touches:** Remove from heat. Stir in the remaining 1 tablespoon of butter and the heavy cream. Taste and adjust salt and sugar if necessary. Garnish generously with fresh cilantro.

## Pro Tips for the Best Murgh Makhani

Achieving restaurant-quality Murgh Makhani at home is within reach with a few expert tips:

*   **Quality Chicken Matters:** Use boneless, skinless chicken thighs for the most tender and juicy results. They hold up better to simmering than breasts.
*   **Don't Skimp on Marination:** The longer the chicken marinates, the more flavorful and tender it will be. Overnight is ideal if you have the time.
*   **Smooth Gravy is Key:** Blending the gravy thoroughly until absolutely smooth is crucial for that signature velvety texture. Soaking cashews beforehand aids in this process and adds richness.
*   **Balance Sweetness and Acidity:** Tomatoes can be quite acidic. A touch of sugar helps balance this, enhancing the overall flavor profile without making the dish overtly sweet.
*   **Kasuri Methi is Essential:** Dried fenugreek leaves (kasuri methi) are non-negotiable for authentic Butter Chicken flavor. Lightly toasting them in a dry pan before crushing and adding them will intensify their aroma.
*   **The Final Touch of Butter and Cream:** Adding the main portions of butter and cream at the very end, off the heat, preserves their delicate flavors and prevents them from splitting.

## Serving Suggestions

Butter Chicken is a versatile dish that pairs wonderfully with a variety of accompaniments, making it a perfect centerpiece for Indian lunch recipes:

*   **Breads:** Warm naan bread (garlic naan is a fantastic choice!), roti, or paratha are ideal for scooping up every last bit of that rich gravy.
*   **Rice:** Steamed basmati rice, jeera rice (cumin rice), or even a simple pulao complements the curry beautifully, soaking up the delicious sauce.
*   **Sides:** A cooling raita (yogurt dip), a fresh kachumber salad (diced cucumber, tomato, onion), or some pickled onions can provide a refreshing contrast to the richness of the Butter Chicken.
*   **Drinks:** A glass of mango lassi (a sweet yogurt drink) or a simple iced tea would be a delightful pairing.

## Variations & Substitutions

While the traditional Butter Chicken recipe is beloved, feel free to experiment with these variations:

*   **Vegetarian Murgh Makhani:** For a meat-free option, substitute chicken with paneer (Indian cottage cheese), tofu, or mixed vegetables like cauliflower and peas. Marinate and cook them similarly before adding to the gravy.
*   **Dairy-Free Version:** Replace yogurt with a plant-based alternative like coconut yogurt for the marinade. For the gravy, use coconut cream instead of heavy cream and a plant-based butter substitute.
*   **Spice Level Adjustment:** For more heat, increase the amount of red chili powder or add a finely chopped green chili to the gravy. For a milder version, reduce the chili powder.
*   **Healthier Twist:** Reduce the amount of butter and cream, or substitute heavy cream with a lighter alternative like half-and-half or even a touch of Greek yogurt (stirred in carefully off the heat to prevent curdling). You can also grill or bake the chicken instead of pan-frying.
*   **Smoky Flavor:** If you have tandoori chicken handy, using it will impart an authentic smoky flavor to your Butter Chicken. Alternatively, a drop of liquid smoke can be added to the gravy.

Butter Chicken is more than just a meal; it's a culinary hug, a dish that brings warmth and satisfaction. Its creamy texture and balanced flavors make it an undisputed champion among Indian lunch recipes, perfect for any occasion. Don't hesitate to try your hand at this beloved classic – your taste buds will thank you!
